record.title: XL330 horn-face joint — Ø16 disc, 4 x M2 on a Ø12 circle, bolted bracket

joins.a: the XL330 servo's horn or idler disc face (part:xl330-m288-t, interface/connector 'horn' or 'idler'): Ø16.0 x 3.0 disc with 4 x Ø1.6 tapped holes 6.0 deep on a Ø12.0 bolt circle
joins.b: the driven bracket's horn face (role 'horn_face' across the microduck shelf: shin 'knee', yaw2roll 'yaw_horn', ankle 'ankle_horn', hip-bracket 'roll_horn'/'pitch_horn', neck-pitch-bracket, yaw-roll-motion, trunk shells): 4 x Ø2.2–2.4 clearance on the same Ø12 circle, usually with Ø4.4 counterbores and a Ø5–6 centre bore

record.dof_left_why: NONE. Four M2 screws through the bracket's clearance holes into the horn's tapped holes clamp the two faces flat; the joint is rigid. THE SERVO'S ROTATION IS NOT THIS JOINT'S — it is the actuator's own, at the part (part:xl330-m288-t; the MJCF's hip/knee/head joints live at the servo). Typing a revolute at a horn mount is the exact mistake connection:spline-servo-25t documents (rc car steering.py:1920) and this folder inherits that rule: mate() never returns a rotation.
record.standard_why: No published standard defines the XL330 horn pattern — it is ROBOTIS's own. Every number here is MEASURED off Pollen's published mesh instead (cecad.meshfeatures on reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/xl330.stl, 2026-09-01: bosses Ø16.0 x 3.0 at x ±13.0; 8 holes Ø1.6 x 6.0 at (y,z) = (0,±6),(±6,0) on both faces = Ø12.0 PCD), with the constants quoted in ce-parts/xl330-m288-t/current/cad/part.py (DISC_D/DISC_L/FACE_D/FACE_PCD/FACE_AT). The Ø1.6 tap is the cecad fasteners.py M2 tap drill, which is what makes the screws M2. `standard: null` is why T4 is not reachable here, and that is correct.
record.adds_parts_why: The joint consumes 4 x M2 cap screws (the horn's 4 tapped holes, measured). ONE ref is named — part:screw-m2-iso4762, the only M2 fastener family with a folder on a reachable shelf (checked 2026-09-02); qty 4 is stated in mate()'s why.adds. Each screw is itself a connection:threaded-m2 joint (thread_ext = the screw, thread_int = the horn's Ø1.6 tapped hole) and an assembly that wants the screws as joints routes them there. The servo itself is NOT added: a connection that mounts a servo is not the reason the servo is in the BOM — the assembly's bom row is.
record.why: The PATTERN is PASS and it is measured on both sides of the joint, not recalled: xl330.stl gives Ø16.0 x 3.0 discs on both faces with 4 x Ø1.6 x 6.0 tapped holes on a Ø12.0 circle (cecad.meshfeatures, 2026-09-01), and ten-plus consumer interfaces on the microduck shelf carry the mirror pattern with their own measured numbers — shin 'knee' 4 x Ø2.2 on an 8.486 mm square (= the same Ø12 circle at the 45-deg positions: the square's diagonal is its bolt circle, 8.486 x sqrt(2) = 12.001), yaw2roll 4 x Ø2.2 on r 6.0 at (±6,0),(0,±6), hip-bracket Ø2.4 on Ø12 with Ø4.84 c'bores. The two spellings (square 8.486 / PCD 12) agree to 0.001 mm. Three things stay CANNOT DETERMINE and are ledger rows, not footnotes: the horn's centre hub (absent from the decimated mesh — axis probe solid, cecad.meshslice 2026-09-02 — while every bracket carries a Ø5–6 centre bore), the clamp/strip torque of 4 M2s in tapped plastic (nothing twisted off in this workshop; the vendor's 0.52 N.m stall via ce-parts/xl330-m288-t is the LOAD to beat, not evidence), and the internal output-spline clocking (mate() carries it as a reported parameter). compat() refuses per-check accordingly.

joint.default_state: assembled: 4 M2 screws fitted and tight. There is no modeled loose state — a horn bracket without its screws is simply off.
joint.why: axes: all six locked — this record's own dof_left. holds_by: PRELOAD — 4 M2 screws clamp the bracket to the horn face; the torque path is the clamped friction plus the screws in shear on the Ø12 circle. driven IS FALSE AND THAT IS THE FIELD DOING THE WORK (the spline-servo-25t rule): a walk that read a driven revolute off a horn mount would put the actuator at the mount instead of inside the servo. The servo's freedom is the part's. transmits: moment, axial and shear — a bolted flange carries all three. rating: screws/pcd/disc/tap are MEASURED (meshfeatures on xl330.stl, quoted in xl330-m288-t part.py); clamp_torque_Nm and hub_pilot_d_mm are MISSING and stay missing — no bench measurement and no hub in the decimated mesh, respectively.
